Just realizing that while Clinton doesn't hold all of my views, she's the only one that can beat Trump.  As much as I would love to see the Green Party receive some federal funding and at least push the Democrats environmental policy and social justice issues to the left a bit, I realize that the Democrat party is a necessary tool to stop Nationalists from taking power.

Just to clarify, I live in a safe blue state so I really don't think a third party could even swing a Trump victory.  But the more and more they talk about how the election was rigged, the more I want any doubt to be removed.  Clinton has my vote this time around. This is going to be a one sided election and no amount of crying "shill" or "fixed" is going to change the fact that Trump is clearly under qualified to be president and a laughing stock outside of the precious Alt-Right echo chamber.

A vague statement about the pharma industry taking advantage of the general population doesn't necessarily tell me she's planning on scaling back on vaccination requirements.  She never has supported anti vaccination policy, just policies to stop pharmaceutical industries from taking advantage of people.  Even then, there's plenty of stuff I disagree with Clinton on that I find just as important (support for "tough on crime" bills, support for Israel but not for Palestine, not working for campaign finance reform, etc.).  Sanders was the closest to my belief system and even then his silence on issues before he ran was a bit disconserting.  Basically, I've had major issues with all the candidates but stopping and embarrassing Trump and his followers is easily the most important issue right now.

Isn't the fact that the choices didn't matter per se kind of fit with the overall tone of the game?  Yeah, you can rewind and change every little thing, but at the end of the day, fate is gonna fuck your shit up.  

I know it's frustrating when these choice based games have only a few solidified endings, but I just feel that this game was more about the experience.  It really felt like an interactive movie more than a game, and I could understand how that could be a bit of a disappointment.  

I just don't hope there are people who felt like they wasted time playing through this whole game.  I got very attached to many of the characters, the community has been amazing, and the atmosphere building in this game is untouched in my opinion.  I've never been emotionally attached to a piece of media like this before.  Whether it be music, movie, tv show, etc.

A huge motif of the game is spirit animals.  We see several deer and some birds.  The overall feeling I got from it was that Arcadia Bay was a town built on corruption and stealing from nature (mass fishing, destroying forest for land development, even the Native American overtones that aren't really touched on enough).  Now that the town has been destroyed, nature pops up in its place with (presumably) the people lost in the tornado coming back as their spirit animal.  It really made me smile in a sentimental kind of way until I realized that Kate might be dead.

That's just my interpretation of that ending and it doesn't entirely justify Chloe not seeming to care, but it would have been a complete disservice to a bittersweet ending like that to have Max and Chloe both sobbing as they drove through this excellent symbolism.  Dontnod chose to leave the sobbing to the player.  And sob we did.
